name: FeedPup – XML & CSV Supplier Feed Import for WooCommerce
author: Weareplano

sections.description:
FeedPup is a WooCommerce supplier feed import tool: it imports products from your supplier’s XML or CSV feed (dropshipping XML, dropshipping CSV or a wholesaler feed) and keeps supplier stock and prices in sync. Paste the supplier feed URL (or upload a CSV file), review the field matches suggested by Pup (FeedPup’s AI-assisted mapper), preview real products, and only then import. After setup, FeedPup updates the selected product details, prices and stock levels on a schedule, so you stop editing spreadsheets by hand.

Supplier feeds all use different field names and structures. FeedPup shows you what it found, and nothing is applied until you confirm it.

Who it’s for: wholesalers, resellers and dropshipping stores that import products from one or more suppliers and need ongoing product sync, stock sync and inventory sync without manual spreadsheet work.

Supplier feed import, supplier stock sync and price sync features

  • AI-assisted field mapping – Pup recognises fields such as titles, SKUs, prices, stock, images and categories and suggests matches, with product examples. You review and confirm every suggestion.
  • Preview before import – Check how products will look in WooCommerce before anything is written.
  • Free draft test import (Basic plan) – Create up to 100 products as WooCommerce drafts to verify the result.
  • Simple and variable products – Import products with their variations and attributes.
  • Category mapping (Growth and Pro) – Map supplier categories to your WooCommerce categories.
  • Price and stock sync – Inventory sync on autopilot: keep selected product details, prices and stock up to date on the schedule your plan includes.
  • Product images – Images are downloaded into your WooCommerce Media Library on import.
  • No needless writes – Unchanged supplier data causes no product writes, and reconnecting reuses linked products.
  • Product-only access – A signed connection that never requests customers, orders, checkout or payment data.

FeedPup uses WooCommerce’s standard stock quantity. Multi-location inventory extensions are not integrated.

Plans

FeedPup is a hosted service (SaaS); nothing in this plugin is locked. Plans are billed by FeedPup via Stripe, and limits are enforced by the service.

  • Basic (free, no time limit): 1 feed, feed analysis, AI-assisted mapping, preview and a test import of up to 100 products as WooCommerce drafts. No full import or scheduled sync.
  • Starter – €9.99/month: 1 feed, up to 750 products, sync every 24 hours.
  • Growth – €19.99/month: up to 3 feeds and 5,000 products, sync every 6 hours, category mapping.
  • Pro – €39.99/month: up to 10 feeds and 20,000 products, sync every 2 hours, priority support.

Yearly billing is available. Each paid plan starts with a 14-day free trial, once per store. Enterprise (agencies, multi-store, large catalogs): contact@weareplano.gr.

Launch offer: 30% off your first 3 months on any paid plan with code LAUNCH30 at checkout.

External services

This plugin connects to the FeedPup hosted service at https://woo.feedpup.weareplano.gr, operated by PLANO (https://weareplano.gr). It is needed to analyse supplier feeds, map fields and run imports and syncs. Nothing is sent until you tick the consent box and click Connect in WooCommerce > FeedPup.

Requests the plugin makes:

  • Connect / Open FeedPup (POST https://woo.feedpup.weareplano.gr/api/wordpress/connect) – when you click Connect FeedPup or Open FeedPup. Sends your site URL, a generated installation ID and a generated connection secret. FeedPup returns a sign-in link to its app.
  • Disconnect (POST https://woo.feedpup.weareplano.gr/api/wordpress/disconnect) – when you click Disconnect FeedPup, or when you deactivate the plugin while connected. Sends the same three values so FeedPup can revoke access and pause syncing.
  • Image downloads – when FeedPup imports a product, the plugin downloads its image URLs from the supplier feed (the supplier’s servers) into your Media Library.

After connecting, FeedPup calls your store’s REST API (/wp-json/feedpup/v1/commerce) with signed requests to read the store name, currency, timezone and plugin version, and to create and update products, variations, prices, stock and categories. It never asks for customer, order, checkout or payment data.

FeedPup stores the supplier feed URL (encrypted), any uploaded CSV file as an encrypted snapshot for up to 7 days (then deleted), the connection secret (encrypted), confirmed mappings, sync preferences, product links, sync results and billing state. For AI-assisted field suggestions, FeedPup may send OpenRouter (https://openrouter.ai) and the model provider serving the request a filtered structural summary of selected feed fields and a small number of sample values. It never sends the full XML feed, the feed URL, the connection secret or payment-card details to AI providers. Paid subscriptions are billed through Stripe-hosted checkout (https://stripe.com); FeedPup does not store card numbers.

  • FeedPup Terms of service: https://woo.feedpup.weareplano.gr/terms
  • FeedPup Privacy policy: https://woo.feedpup.weareplano.gr/privacy
  • OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai/terms and https://openrouter.ai/privacy
  • Stripe: https://stripe.com/legal and https://stripe.com/privacy

Data retention and removal

  • Disconnect: the local connection secret is deleted, FeedPup revokes access and pauses syncing. Feed settings and product links are kept for up to 30 days to allow reconnection, then deleted. Imported products stay in your store.
  • Deactivate: the plugin asks FeedPup to revoke access and starts the same retention period. If FeedPup cannot be reached, the local secret is still deleted, so no more signed writes are possible.
  • Uninstall: plugin settings and the local secret are removed. Four small feedpup_* tables holding product IDs and keys are kept so a reinstall can recognise linked products instead of duplicating them. If you will never use FeedPup again, you can drop them manually.
  • FeedPup never deletes your WooCommerce products, variations, categories, images or orders.
  • Disconnecting or uninstalling does not cancel a paid subscription. Cancel it in FeedPup’s billing controls first.

Support

Email contact@weareplano.gr with your store address and, if relevant, when the problem happened. Don’t email feed URLs that contain credentials.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce (8.0 or later).
  2. Go to Plugins > Add New, search for “FeedPup”, install and activate it. Or upload the feedpup-xml-supplier-sync-for-woocommerce folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  3. Make sure pretty permalinks are on (Settings > Permalinks, any option except “Plain”) and your store has a public HTTPS address.
  4. Open WooCommerce > FeedPup, read the connection and data-use notice, tick the consent box and click Connect FeedPup.
  5. FeedPup opens in a separate tab. Paste your supplier XML or CSV feed URL (or upload a CSV file) and analyse it.
  6. Review the suggested mappings, preview products and run the free draft test import (Basic plan, up to 100 products).
  7. Choose a paid plan only when you are ready for a full import or scheduled sync.

Requirements: WordPress 6.3+, PHP 8.1+, WooCommerce 8.0+, pretty permalinks, and a public HTTPS store URL.
sections.faq:
How do I import products from an XML or CSV feed into WooCommerce?

Open WooCommerce > FeedPup and connect, paste the supplier XML or CSV feed URL (or upload a CSV) in the FeedPup app, confirm the suggested field mapping, preview the products and run the free draft test import (up to 100 draft products on the Basic plan). A full import is one click after that on a paid plan.

Can FeedPup update stock and prices from a supplier feed automatically?

Yes. After the first import, scheduled syncs update the stock quantity, prices and other fields you selected: every 24 hours on Starter, every 6 hours on Growth and every 2 hours on Pro. A run with no supplier changes makes no product writes.

Does it work with a dropshipping XML, dropshipping CSV or wholesaler feed?

Yes, as long as the supplier provides an XML or CSV product feed. FeedPup is built for feeds that use their own field names and structures. Check your feed with the free analysis and preview first.

Can I import a CSV file?

Yes. Paste a CSV or TSV feed URL (comma, semicolon or tab separated; the format is detected automatically) or upload a CSV file of up to 5 MB. Uploaded files are snapshots, so automatic sync needs a feed URL that your supplier keeps updated.

Which suppliers work? Can I use any XML supplier feed or CSV supplier file?

Any supplier that gives you a product feed as XML, or as CSV/TSV (comma, semicolon or tab separated), via a URL, or a CSV file you upload. FeedPup does not need a supplier-specific integration: it reads the feed’s own field names and suggests mappings that you confirm. Use the free analysis and preview to check your feed.

Does supplier stock sync and supplier price sync run automatically?

Yes, on a paid plan with a feed URL. Each scheduled sync updates the stock quantity (using WooCommerce’s standard stock functions), prices and the other fields you selected for the products FeedPup imported.

What happens to products already in my store?

FeedPup does not overwrite or delete them. It creates and updates only the products it imported and linked. If a supplier SKU already exists in your store, the new product gets a unique SKU suffix instead of overwriting the existing one. FeedPup never deletes WooCommerce products.

How often does it sync?

Every 24 hours on Starter, every 6 hours on Growth and every 2 hours on Pro. The free Basic plan has no scheduled sync.

What are the limits on each plan?

  • Basic (free): 1 feed, analysis, mapping, preview and a draft test import of up to 100 products.
  • Starter (€9.99/month): 1 feed, up to 750 products, sync every 24 hours.
  • Growth (€19.99/month): up to 3 feeds and 5,000 products, sync every 6 hours, category mapping.
  • Pro (€39.99/month): up to 10 feeds and 20,000 products, sync every 2 hours, priority support.

How is FeedPup different from WP All Import?

WP All Import is a general-purpose importer for many kinds of WordPress content that runs inside your site, where you build the import template yourself. FeedPup focuses only on WooCommerce supplier product feeds: it is a hosted service that suggests the field mapping with AI, shows a product preview, lets you test with draft products, and then keeps prices and stock in sync on a schedule.

Does FeedPup import products without asking?

No. You review the detected fields and preview first. The free test import creates draft products, and a full import starts only when you choose it.

Is this an automatic product import tool?

FeedPup automates the recurring work. You confirm the mapping and start the first import yourself; after that, scheduled syncs keep the linked products’ prices, stock and selected fields up to date automatically on a paid plan.

What is the difference between XML import and CSV import?

None in how you work with FeedPup. Both formats go through the same mapping, preview and test import steps. Use a feed URL for either format if you want automatic stock sync.

Can I try it before paying?

Yes. The Basic plan is free with no time limit and includes a draft test import of up to 100 products. Every paid plan starts with a 14-day free trial.

Is my product data sent to an AI service?

Only a filtered structural summary of selected feed fields and a few sample values are used for AI suggestions. The full feed or uploaded file, the feed URL, your connection secret and payment details are never sent to AI providers. See “External services” below.

What happens if my feed has more products than my plan allows?

The full import stops before writing and asks you to upgrade; nothing is partially imported. Each variation counts toward the plan’s product limit.

Is FeedPup available in my language?

The plugin is translation-ready. Translations are delivered as WordPress.org language packs; you can help at translate.wordpress.org.

How do I change or cancel a paid plan?

Open Plans in FeedPup and use the hosted billing controls. Disconnecting the plugin does not cancel a paid subscription.
sections.changelog:
0.1.3

  • Compatibility: tested with WooCommerce 11.2 and WordPress 7.1.

0.1.2

  • Listing: plugin name and readme updated for clarity.
  • Security: signed FeedPup REST requests are now authenticated in the route’s permission callback.
  • Security: the service address is fixed to the official FeedPup host; the editable service URL setting was removed.
  • Stock updates now use WooCommerce’s wc_update_product_stock() instead of direct database writes.
  • Added Plugin URI and License URI headers.

Older releases: see changelog.txt.
